title: Parameter type conversion and validation callpath
answers: How does Click convert raw CLI argument strings into typed Python values?
What is the control flow from Parameter initialization to ParamType.convert?
How does ParamType report parsing and validation errors during command execution?
body:
`src/click/core.py:Parameter.__init__` calls `src/click/types.py:convert_type` to convert user-specified types (native types like `int`, tuple literals, or default value fallbacks) into a `ParamType` instance.
During command execution, `src/click/core.py:Parameter.type_cast_value` invokes `src/click/types.py:ParamType.__call__` with the parsed token, parameter, and context.
`src/click/types.py:ParamType.__call__` delegates directly to `src/click/types.py:ParamType.convert` for coercion and validation.
On failure, `src/click/types.py:ParamType.fail` formats the error message and raises `src/click/exceptions.py:BadParameter` to stop execution and produce a CLI error message.
says: Passing non-numeric text into a number field causes unclear command line errors.
The terminal does not properly translate user input text into structured data.
Show user-friendly error messages when argument values cannot be parsed correctly.
Converting user-supplied flag arguments into expected formats fails without clear explanation.
Provide clear feedback when a supplied option value fails format validation checks.
